title: No Verified Incident: Dog-Trade Claims Need Public Records
excerpt: No police seizure, court judgment, or health alert is documented here. Public demands need proof, quarantine, and a clear route to abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No verified police seizure, court judgment, intercepted shipment, or emergency health alert accompanies this material. That gap matters. Claims about stolen companions, poison bait, farm-raised dogs, and contaminated meat cannot become fact through repetition. Families, pet owners, and communities deserve records strong enough to support action.

Myths need records, not slogans

“Farm-raised” cannot be tested by assertion. A credible supply chain needs traceable ownership, transport documents, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and enforcement records. None are identified here. Without those records, no honest account can prove how animals entered trade, whether they were stolen, or whether transport rules were followed.

Public health demands precision

Rabies risk concerns infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once symptoms develop, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. See WHO guidance.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains remain separate questions. Both require competent surveillance, quarantine, and enforcement. Evidence must lead reform, not excuses.

Demand a lawful end

Vietnamese families and communities can demand protection for people and companion animals. SDE calls for complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.
author: SDE Research Team
